q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Net ROAS rose modestly in early October while net profit worsened — net ROAS increased ~+5.9% (Oct 1–13 vs Sep), but net profit moved from a loss of ₹5,741/day to a loss of ₹8,108/day (≈+41% worse).

Evidence
- ROAS and its levers (Oct 1–13 vs Sep 1–30)
  - Net ROAS: ~0.83x (period avg); net ROAS change split: contribution margin per order ↑11% (helping ROAS +11.3%) while ad‑spend per order ↑5% (pushing ROAS −4.9%) → net effect +5.9%.
- Why net profit fell (same comparison)
  - Net profit per day: loss ₹5,741 → loss ₹8,108 per day (+41% worse).
  - Net COGS per day: ₹22,541 → ₹31,334 (+39%).
  - Refunds per day: ₹19,009 → ₹23,507 (+24%).
  - Ad spend per day: ₹44,197 → ₹54,529 (+23%).
- Platform context: both Meta and Google increased spend and orders; CPC/CPM fell sharply while volumes rose, so ROI per rupee on ads improved modestly but absolute costs (COGS, refunds, ad spend) rose enough to deepen losses.

Period: 2026-10-01..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
